hints.S45_A1: 'As ___ as' is a simile, and the streets are LIT UP and compared with A THOUSAND STARS. Ask: are stars loud, or empty, or shining? Match the adjective to the stars, never to the crowd.
hints.S45_A2: Shoes must come away from your feet BEFORE ENTERING THE TEMPLE - that is what visitors do at a place of worship. Ask: which phrasal verb means to remove shoes or clothing? 'Wash' cleans them; 'repair' mends them.
hints.S45_A3: The LARGE TABLE OF FOOD OFFERINGS was set out neatly and PLACED OUTSIDE THEIR DOOR for the new year. Ask: which verb means to put things into careful order? 'Removed' and 'destroyed' would leave nothing there.
hints.S45_A4: The dash explains it: RELATIVES FROM ACROSS THE ISLAND GATHERED FOR THE FIRST TIME IN YEARS. Ask: does that feel dull, ordinary or silent - or full of happiness? Match the adjective to the reunion.
hints.S45_A5: The CHRISTMAS CHOIR sang so beautifully that PEOPLE PASSING ON THE STREET STOPPED TO LISTEN. Ask: which noun names voices blending perfectly together? 'Silence' and 'confusion' would empty the street instead.
hints.S45_B1: The subject is EVERYONE, not the neighbourhood around it. Words like everyone and nobody behave like ONE person. Ask: in the simple present, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the one carrying -s?
hints.S45_B2: HAS is waiting for its partner, and SINCE I WAS VERY YOUNG runs right up to now. Ask: after 'has', which form builds a present perfect? 'Make' is irregular, so no -ed ending will do.
hints.S45_B3: FAR needs a comparative to lean on, and THAN sets THIS YEAR against THE ONE LAST YEAR - just two displays. Ask: does a three-syllable adjective take -er, or a comparing word in front? 'The most' would need several displays.
hints.S45_B4: THE PARADE SUDDENLY STARTED EARLY - a sharp event landing in the middle of something longer. Ask: which choice shows the children already busy with their TRADITIONAL COSTUMES at that past moment?
hints.S45_B5: FOOD cannot be counted - there is no plural - and the result clause (THAT WE COULD NOT TRY EVERYTHING) tells you the amount was huge. Ask: which choice suits an uncountable noun inside that frame? 'A few' and 'several' need countable things.
hints.S45_B6: The statement is already NEGATIVE (NOT NERVOUS AT ALL) and it sits in the past. Ask: after a negative statement, does the tag flip to positive or stay negative? The tag must keep the past tense, so 'are' cannot appear.
hints.S45_B7: The giant COSTUME cannot move itself: TEN SKILLED PERFORMERS do the work, and the parade is over. Ask: which choice is passive, with the subject receiving the action, and set in the past?
hints.S45_B8: The organiser is FORBIDDING FLASH PHOTOGRAPHY near the RELIGIOUS OFFERINGS. Ask: after 'told + person', does a plain verb follow, an -ing form, or an infinitive with its marker? And where does the negative word sit?
hints.S45_C1: HOW stands just in front of the blank, and FESTIVALS can be counted one by one. Ask: which quantity word partners countable plurals in a question? Its twin word belongs to things you cannot count, like EXCITEMENT.
hints.S45_C2: EXCITEMENT cannot be counted - it has no plural - and the fixed frame is 'so ___ ... THAT even the streets seem to sparkle'. Ask: which single quantity word fits an uncountable noun inside that frame?
hints.S45_C3: The sentence is POSITIVE: Mother really did prepare kueh and OFFERED A PLATE TO EVERYONE who walked past. Ask: which box word states an unstated amount in a positive statement? Its twin belongs to negatives and questions.
hints.S45_C4: Read the whole clause: I DID NOT EAT ... AT ALL - it is negative, and not even one tart was touched. Ask: which box word partners negatives and questions? Its positive twin cannot follow 'did not'.
hints.S45_C5: Count them: JUST THREE candles, and candles can be counted one by one. Ask: which box phrase means only two or three countable things? 'Several' would mean more, and 'little' belongs to things you cannot count.
hints.S45_C6: ROSEWATER is liquid, so you cannot count it, and the clue NO MORE THAN says the quantity is tiny. Ask: which box phrase names small amounts that cannot be counted? Countable phrases belong with candles, not with liquid.
hints.S45_C7: The dash counts them: FIVE IN A SINGLE AFTERNOON - more than two or three, but hardly a crowd. Ask: which box word names that middle number of countable things? 'A few' would stop at three.
hints.S45_C8: LAUGHTER AND SINGING went on until very late - that is plenty, not scarcity, and the sentence is positive. Ask: which box phrase means large quantities in positive statements, countable or not? 'Much' sounds unnatural here.
hints.S45_D1: The blank is paired with AND TRADITIONS, so it names something similar: practices handed down for generations. Ask: which box word names those long-standing ways of doing things? After 'rich' it must be plural.
hints.S45_D2: The blank follows 'families', so it must be a verb, and the clue is OIL LAMPS AND COLOURFUL KOLAM PATTERNS on the home. Ask: which box word means to make a place look festive?
hints.S45_D3: The clue is WORSHIPPERS CARRYING OFFERINGS, MOVING THROUGH THE STREETS in one organised line. Ask: which box word names that slow ceremonial march? 'Customs' are practices, not a moving group of people.
hints.S45_D4: The dash defines it: THANKFULNESS FOR FAMILY AND THE BLESSINGS OF THE YEAR. Ask: which box word names that feeling? 'Unity' is about people joining together, not about giving thanks.
hints.S45_D5: The dash explains it: DIFFERENT PEOPLES COMING TOGETHER AS ONE NATION. Ask: which box word names that state of being joined into one? 'Customs' differ from group to group; this is what they all share.
hints.S45_E1: Count the subject: THE LANTERNS GLOWING SOFTLY along the corridor - more than one. Ask: does a plural subject take a singular past verb, or a plural one? The corridor is not the subject.
hints.S45_E2: Test it: WE SAT ___ ON A MAT - can you say 'at that place'? Nobody owns the mat. Ask: which spelling names a place, and which one means 'belonging to them'?
hints.S45_E3: Grandmother holds this opinion about the FESTIVAL OF LIGHTS, but the underlined word has two letters swapped. Ask: does the rule say I before E, or E before I, when no C stands in front? Compare: relief, field, piece.
hints.S45_E4: PLACED is an action verb, and the underlined word tells you HOW she placed each OIL LAMP. Ask: do we describe an action with an adjective, or with an adverb ending in -ly?
hints.S45_E5: It HAS ALWAYS BEEN OUR ___ TRADITION - one family owns this custom. Ask: can a plain -s ever show ownership? Decide where the apostrophe belongs when a single owner is named.
hints.S45_F1: Sentence A is the condition: you VISIT YOUR NEIGHBOURS during Hari Raya. Ask: after a condition phrase, does the verb take 'will', or stay in the simple present? Save the future for the second half - the bond that grows.
hints.S45_F2: Both sentences describe THE DEEPAVALI PARADE, so name it once and let 'which' take over the second mention. Ask: after 'which', is the word 'it' still needed? And what punctuation fences off the extra information?
